claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game gets repetitive after extended play sessions.

citations.review_text: kinda repetitive but fun with friends and a mic

I have played Insurgency: Sandstorm for around 20 hours, and the gunplay is easily the best part of the game. It feels intense, realistic, and really satisfying. Every weapon has weight to it, and firefights can get chaotic very quickly.

I also really enjoyed the Player vs. Bot mode. It is a great option when you want tactical action without having to deal with sweaty PvP matches all the time. The game can become a little repetitive after a while, though, especially if you keep playing the same modes.

I would definitely recommend it to people who enjoy realistic shooters. However, if you want something even more extreme in terms of realism, there are games like Bodycam. Still, Insurgency: Sandstorm is a very fun and solid tactical shooter.

single_points.text: One reviewer says when gear is allowed or not allowed to be equipped is very difficult to understand and not intuitive at all.

citation.review_text:
Too many bugs and problems:

Fire on ground will burn you in an area wider than the actual fire. Helicopters with miniguns will shoot you through foot thick stone walls. Insurgency suicider bombers will explode and kill you despite being on the other side of a big obstacle. Armored enemies can tank sometimes +5 shots of the highest calibers without flinching running straight up to you and instakill you with melee. Getting hit by the "blast" of a molotov cocktail instakills you even if you are in the perifery of the explosion.

When gear is allowed or not allowed to be equipped is very difficult to understand and not intuitive at all. It seems that different missions will sometimes have different loadout, or the loadout will change, or a lot of gear is not able to be selected. And you never get any explanation why this is so.

When you join a match you may have to wait up to 4 minutes before the other players clear an objective and you are actually allowed to play.

.... etc etc.

Graphics are fairly plain and not up to 2018 standards, when the game got released. It's not terrible, it just feels like its graphics was already obsolete even for 2018.

claims.claim: Matchmaking frequently drops players into ongoing matches that are already halfway complete or nearing their end.

citations.review_text:
The gameplay itself is exceptionally well done, it's more realistic than just about any shooter I've played, very fun, and the coop element is well done, can't say much about PvP as I don't really care about that.

However, while the gameplay and game design are great, their infrastructure is ABOMINABLE and someone needs to get fired ASAP. Assume that roughly 1 in 5 games will terminate either by the server dropping everyone or by making everyone lag so hard there's nothing left to do but leave. I don't know what kind of potato farms they're labeling as servers, but they suck ass.

The matchmaking also leaves  a lot to be desired, the only thing you can do is queue up, you can't filter which maps/lighting settings you want, can't choose to start a new match, most of the time you'll just be thrown into whatever match is already underway, half the time right as it ends, other times you'll have to wait 2-3 minutes to actually be spawned in because the team needs to capture an objective to respawn you. The wait is fine, but getting tossed into matches that are halfway through gets annoying fast.

I strongly recommend this game only if you're willing to run your own servers or know someone who does, community servers work very well, server hosting is fairly simple, but their own servers are absolute ass

claims.claim: Voice chat channels frequently feature toxic and racist behavior from other players.

citations.review_text:
Not sure what it is about insurgency...

Gunplay is excellent all around, TTK is extremely short, maps and movement are great, fire support is really enjoyable and when your lobbies click, well that just ties it all together. That said, this game is dying, and the prime reason why is because it's community sucks.

The people with thousands of hours in insurgency seem to be some of the most unforgiving, toxic, unhelpful, and genuinely angry people that I have ever played games with. Matches are long, team play is important, and communication is paramount. So when you have a toxic, racist, deeply angry individual on your team, the game suffers, and the player base leaves. I like everything about this game except for the moderation. It's genuinely the wild west out there, which can result in a beautiful experience where the team excels independent of the individual. But in my experience about 7/10 games result in someone spouting racism, toxicity, and other forms of hate into voip. Mute works, sure but at the end of the day if you remove communication from insurgency, you lose what makes the game good.

I really want to love this game, but the lack of moderation and the absolutely terrible community prevent me from giving it a recommendation in 2026. Maybe it was different when there were more players, but as it stands now, let the assholes have their game.

Great guns and graphics with fun gameplay that are ruined by an army of racist, moronic kids and a lack of game mode variety in a game with an already shrunk playerbase (why is there no deathmatch). Maybe start by monitoring VC and removing racist filth from your game to show some respect towards it. These 4chan edgelords are being mass produced because no one knows how to raise good kids anymore.

You’re not getting any new players if the game is mostly just waiting simulator cake with racist icing..

claims.claim: Players experience frequent connection losses, server lag, and being placed back into matches they just left.

citations.review_text: Trash since other devs took over. dead game, cheaters, high ping.
tried it again. you people cant seem to fix the lag in this game.

I wish Steam had a sideways thumb, because I've never had such a love-hate relationship with a game.

Ever since they introduced cross-platform play, the connection issues have been absolutely insane. They existed before, but they've gotten significantly worse.

I actually jumped back on today after taking a long break and decided to try the new CHAD666 content.

First game? Connection lost.

Second game? Connection lost.

There's nothing quite like being deep into a match, having a great time, and suddenly noticing everyone running endlessly into walls. You know exactly what's coming next. It's infuriating.

After 30 minutes, I uninstalled the game again.

Here's the thing, though. I have over 500 hours in *Insurgency: Sandstorm*, so I'm certainly not going to pretend I haven't gotten my money's worth. When the game actually works, it's fantastic. The gunplay is excellent, the atmosphere is intense, and the developers consistently release new content. There's a lot to love here.

But you know what I'd love even more than new content? **Being able to play the damn game without getting disconnected.**

That's what makes this so frustrating. Underneath all these connection issues is a genuinely great shooter that I've spent hundreds of hours enjoying. I want to keep playing it, but the game seems determined not to let me.

So, the thumbs-up is for the 500 hours of great memories and the genuinely fantastic gameplay.

The thumbs-down is for the current state of the servers and the fact that I can't seem to finish a match without getting disconnected.

**Final verdict: 👍👎 — I love this game. I also hate this game. And apparently, the servers hate me.**
